newsitem.title: UK: IBCA affirms Tunisia's long-term BBB minus rating.
newsitem.headline: IBCA affirms Tunisia's long-term BBB minus rating.

text.p: IBCA, the European rating agency, said on Friday it affirmed the long-term foreign currency rating of Tunisia at BBB minus.
IBCA also affirmed Tunisia's short-term A3 rating.
"Tunisia maintains a good track record for sound fiscal and monetary policy which has tamed public finances and inflation and resulted in a stable currency," IBCA said in a statement.
"Combined with reforms, good macro-economic management helped diversify the economy and increase its resilience to shocks," it said.
The agency said that despite a protracted drought from 1993 to 1995 -- which put pressure on prices, imports and government finances -- the economy still posted positive growth.
"Tunisia has shown further commitment to reform, which was started in 1986, by signing an Association agreement with the EU, IBCA said.

"The agreement involves the gradual removal of the remaining barriers to trade and is expected to lead to a free trade area in twelve years time. Businesses, under government leadership, are preparing for the challenge."

But IBCA said Tunsia's trade deficit was still high relative to GDP and its financing relied heavily on tourism receipts and workers' remittances, both of which are very sensitive to external political developments.
IBCA said that while Tunisia's debt service record was "impeccable", political risk was holding the country's rating down.

"The past year has been marked by increased intolerance of political dissent. Yet, internal political risk is mitigated by the near eradication of the Islamist threat and by social programmes which have ensured rising prosperity, thus pre-empting social unrest," it said.
"However, the recent political developments have raised the stakes -- should the economy falter, political unrest may surface," IBCA said.
